key_findings.detail: StormCast autoregressively predicts 99 state variables at km-scale using HRRR (3km CONUS) as its training target, with dense vertical resolution in the atmospheric boundary layer and a 1-hour timestep. Weights are open on HuggingFace, training recipe is documented via NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo, inference via Earth2Studio, licensed under NVIDIA's Open Model License (commercial-use permitted). This is the single closest match in the entire search to 'sub-10km resolution, fine-tunable' — everything else needs an added downscaling stage.

key_findings.finding: No standalone weather model exists on HuggingFace with an out-of-the-box sub-10km global resolution; km-scale requires a two-stage global-model + downscaler pipeline
key_findings.detail: Recent literature converges on the same pattern: take a pretrained global backbone (GraphCast/FourCastNet/Aurora-class) and add a second, purpose-built downscaling/super-resolution model conditioned on topography to reach terrain scale. Named systems found: NVIDIA CorrDiff (diffusion downscaling to km-scale regional fields, part of open Earth-2), FuXi-CFD (terrain-informed 3D wind fields at 30m from coarse inputs), SpLIIF (implicit-function downscaling to sub-km from sparse stations+topography, beats CorrDiff on temperature by up to 50%), AirCast-SR (diffusion foundation model for km-scale super-resolution of 0.25° AI forecasts), and a station-focused approach ('Partial recovery of meter-scale surface weather,' arXiv 2602.23146) that trains directly against 11,000 US weather stations plus ERA5 + satellite data to produce 10m-resolution micro-weather fields — the most directly comparable published approach to fine-tuning with station-level observations.

key_findings.finding: WeatherBench 2 is a benchmark/eval framework, not itself a source of pretrained weights
key_findings.source: github.com/google-research/weatherbench2, sites.research.google/gr/weatherbench
key_findings.detail: WeatherBench 2 provides open, cloud-optimized ERA5 ground truth, baseline datasets, and an open-source evaluation framework plus a continuously updated public leaderboard comparing GraphCast, Pangu, FourCastNet, NeuralGCM, GenCast, HRES and ENS on identical metrics. Useful as the evaluation harness once a terrain-scale model is built, and as a pointer to which upstream global model currently has the best skill to fine-tune from, but it does not host downloadable model weights itself.

models.name: GraphCast / WeatherNext Graph (Google DeepMind)
models.description: Encoder-processor-decoder graph neural network for deterministic medium-range global forecasting; 0.25° resolution, 37 pressure levels, trained on ERA5 1979-2017.
models.architecture: Graph Neural Network (icosahedral mesh, encoder-processor-decoder)
models.transferable: Fine-tuning code exists but no full training infra officially released; community has fine-tuned it onto regional NWP analyses (Subich 2024) at the same resolution/grid. Weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial only).

models.name: GenCast / WeatherNext Gen (Google DeepMind)
models.description: Diffusion-based probabilistic ensemble weather model, 0.25° resolution, outperforms ECMWF ENS on medium-range extreme-event risk.
models.architecture: Conditional diffusion model over a graph/mesh representation
models.transferable: Weights/code released alongside GraphCast in the same repo; same CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 non-commercial weight license.

models.name: Pangu-Weather (Huawei)
models.description: 3D Earth-Specific Transformer for global weather forecasting at four lead times (1/3/6/24hr), 0.25° resolution, with native topography/land/soil static-input conditioning.
models.architecture: 3D Earth-Specific Transformer (Swin-style 3D attention)
models.source: github.com/198808xc/Pangu-Weather (ONNX weights via Google Drive/Baidu); mirrors on HuggingFace (OneScience-Group/Pangu_Weather) and PyTorch reimplementation (Helmholtz-AI-Energy/pangu_weather)
models.transferable: PyTorch reimplementations expose load_pretrained_weights() for fine-tuning; NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo also ships a trainable re-implementation. Explicit topography conditioning is a useful precedent for terrain-aware fine-tuning.

models.name: FourCastNet / FourCastNet3 (NVIDIA)
models.description: Global data-driven forecast model using Adaptive/Spherical Fourier Neural Operator attention; FourCastNet3 adds scalable probabilistic ensemble forecasting.
models.architecture: Vision Transformer with AFNO (v1) / Spherical Fourier Neural Operator (v2/v3)
models.transferable: Apache 2.0 / NVIDIA Open Model License, commercially usable. AFNO/SFNO blocks are architecturally simple and reusable as a generic spectral-attention feature extractor outside the weather task.

models.name: StormCast (NVIDIA)
models.description: Mesoscale diffusion-based model autoregressively predicting 99 state variables at km-scale resolution over CONUS, trained on 3km HRRR data with dense boundary-layer vertical resolution.
models.architecture: Diffusion model (regional, km-scale)
models.transferable: Best-suited of all models found here as a starting point genuinely near terrain scale; training recipe is published, and NVIDIA Open Model License permits commercial derivative models.

models.name: CorrDiff (NVIDIA Earth-2)
models.description: Generative diffusion model that downscales coarse continental-scale AI forecasts to high-resolution regional/km-scale fields, ~500x faster than traditional dynamical downscaling.
models.architecture: Conditional diffusion / residual correction model
models.source: NVIDIA Earth-2 model family (build.nvidia.com, NGC catalog)
models.transferable: Purpose-built as the second-stage downscaler to pair with a global backbone (e.g. FourCastNet, GraphCast) for terrain-scale output; open under NVIDIA's Earth-2 open model license.

models.name: ClimaX (Microsoft Research)
models.description: First general-purpose foundation model for weather & climate; variable-agnostic ViT encoder pretrained on CMIP6, with documented fine-tuning recipes for forecasting and climate downscaling.
models.architecture: Vision Transformer with variable/positional tokenization
models.transferable: MIT licensed, explicitly designed and documented for fine-tuning to downstream tasks including downscaling, but pretraining resolution (1.4-5.6°) is far coarser than terrain-scale needs — best used as an architecture/training-recipe reference rather than a direct backbone.

models.name: Aurora (Microsoft Research)
models.description: Foundation model for the Earth system covering atmosphere, air pollution, and ocean waves; several checkpoints at 0.25° (and finer for specialized tasks).
models.architecture: 3D Swin Transformer-based encoder-decoder, perceiver-style variable encoding
models.transferable: Checkpoint-loading API supports arbitrary fine-tuned weights from an HF repo, making fine-tuning mechanically easy, but license is restrictive ('Other' on GitHub; Microsoft requires direct contact for commercial use) — confirm licensing before committing to it.

models.name: NeuralGCM (Google Research)
models.description: Hybrid machine-learning + physics general circulation model; couples a differentiable dynamical core with learned physics parameterizations.
models.architecture: Hybrid: differentiable spectral dynamical core + neural network subgrid physics
models.transferable: Apache 2.0 code, CC BY-SA 4.0 weights (commercially usable with attribution/share-alike). Less suited as a pure learned 'feature extractor' since a meaningful share of its skill comes from the embedded physics solver rather than a purely learned representation.

models.name: Prithvi-WxC (NASA / IBM)
models.description: 2.3B-parameter transformer foundation model for weather and climate, pretrained on 40 years of MERRA-2 reanalysis, explicitly designed for downstream fine-tuning to specialized tasks.
models.architecture: Transformer (masked autoencoder-style pretraining) with local+global attention over atmospheric fields
models.transferable: Purpose-built as a fine-tunable foundation model with a dedicated fine-tuning-applications repo family; active research (2025) on adapting it from its native MERRA-2 resolution toward finer ERA5-class resolution — the closest existing precedent for adapting toward station-level terrain data. Openly licensed for open science use.

models.name: Prithvi-EO (NASA / IBM)
models.description: Geospatial foundation model pretrained on Harmonized Landsat/Sentinel-2 (HLS) Earth observation imagery — not a weather model, but usable as a source of terrain/land-cover embeddings.
models.architecture: Vision Transformer (masked autoencoder, ViT-based)
models.transferable: Recent literature (arXiv 2608.12271) uses EO foundation-model embeddings as sub-grid terrain/land-surface descriptors to condition a downscaling model — i.e. best paired alongside a weather backbone (feeding it terrain features) rather than used alone for weather prediction.

models.name: AIFS (ECMWF)
models.description: ECMWF's own operational-grade AI Forecasting System, an encoder-processor-decoder model comparable in class to GraphCast/Pangu, produced by the agency that generates the ERA5/HRES reference data.
models.architecture: Graph-transformer encoder-processor-decoder
models.transferable: Fully open weights under CC BY 4.0 (no non-commercial restriction, unlike GraphCast/GenCast/Aurora) — the most licensing-friendly of the top-tier global backbones, and comes from the same institution that produces the verification/reanalysis data used to score everything else.

models.name: Atlas (NVIDIA)
models.description: Generative AI ensemble model autoregressively predicting ERA5 variables on a 0.25° global grid, released January 2026.
models.architecture: Generative (diffusion/GAN-class, per NVIDIA Earth-2 family conventions)
models.transferable: Newest addition to NVIDIA's Earth-2 open model family; same commercially-usable NVIDIA Open Model License as FourCastNet3/StormCast.

datasets.name: Swiss IMIS Network (SLF)
datasets.description: Intercantonal Measurement and Information System: ~180-200 automatic high-alpine stations across the Swiss Alps and Jura, mostly above treeline (2000-3000m), near avalanche starting zones. 30-min measurement interval.
datasets.variables: Snow depth, new snow (HS/HN), air temp, RH, wind speed/dir, snow surface temp; some stations also have Snowpack model outputs
datasets.density: ~180-200 stations across ~41,000 km2 of Alps -> sparse nationally (avg spacing >10km) but locally dense within specific massifs/valleys where multiple stations cluster (e.g. ski-area regions can have several within 1-5km)

datasets.name: MeteoSwiss SwissMetNet / Open Data (OGD)
datasets.description: National automatic weather station network, ~158-160 full stations plus ~100 precipitation-only stations, covering all Swiss altitude levels; STAC-based REST API on the Federal Spatial Data Infrastructure.
datasets.variables: Temperature, precipitation, wind, pressure, snow, humidity, sunshine duration, radiation
datasets.density: ~160 full stations nationally; denser in Alpine valleys/passes than in lowlands but still generally >5km spacing except in a few clusters

datasets.name: PeakWeather (MeteoSwiss ML benchmark dataset)
datasets.description: Purpose-built, benchmark-ready dataset for spatiotemporal deep learning derived from MeteoSwiss's own ground network, released with topographical indices per station specifically to support terrain-aware ML weather modeling.
datasets.variables: Full surface met variables at 10-min resolution plus topographic indices (elevation, slope, aspect, terrain complexity metrics) per station
datasets.density: 302 station locations across Switzerland's complex topography, >8 years of 10-min data — already curated for terrain-weather ML, the single most directly usable dataset found

datasets.name: GeoSphere Austria / ZAMG Meteorological Network
datasets.description: Austria's national network, described by the operator as one of the densest meteorological networks worldwide, covering all climate regions and altitudes including alpine terrain.
datasets.variables: Temperature, precipitation, wind, radiation, humidity, pressure (TAWES 10-min raw + QC'd Stationsdaten-v2 hourly/daily/monthly)
datasets.density: >250 stations nationwide (some sources cite 271 TAWES stations); Austria's mountainous terrain means many station pairs fall within a few km in valley/ridge systems, though not uniformly at 1-5km

datasets.name: WegenerNet Feldbach & Gesäuse Regions (Austria)
datasets.description: Purpose-built ultra-dense hydrometeorological climate-station network designed explicitly to resolve the 1-10km spatial scale; Feldbach region (Alpine foreland, 22x16km) plus a Gesäuse mountain-region extension.
datasets.variables: Temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, pressure, radiation (plus 3D observing systems: profiling)
datasets.density: ~155 stations over ~350 km2 (~1 station per 2 km2, near-1km average spacing) in Feldbach, plus ~20 additional stations in the mountainous Gesäuse region — the single densest true in-situ network found in this search

datasets.name: EEAR-Clim (Extended European Alpine Region)
datasets.description: A new (2024-2025) harmonized high-density daily observational dataset merging multiple national/regional station networks across the greater Alpine region (France to Hungary) specifically to overcome the limited spatial coverage of prior Alpine climate products.
datasets.variables: Daily precipitation and air temperature
datasets.density: Described as 'very dense' pan-Alpine network aggregation; local spacing varies by source network but is markedly denser than any single national network alone, covering ~800,000 km2

datasets.name: Reynolds Creek Experimental Watershed / Critical Zone Observatory
datasets.description: USDA-ARS outdoor hydrological laboratory in Idaho with 60+ years of instrumentation; includes a published 21TB gridded hourly product (air temp, RH, precip amount/phase) interpolated from station network onto a 10m LiDAR DEM using detrended kriging that explicitly encodes terrain effects.
datasets.variables: Air temperature, RH, precipitation amount & phase, vapor pressure, radiation, wind
datasets.density: 35 meteorological sites across a 238 km2 mesoscale basin (~2.6km average spacing) spanning the rain-snow transition zone; the gridded 10m product is a strong ready-made terrain-weather-physics target

datasets.name: Senator Beck Basin / Mountain System Monitoring (CSAS)
datasets.description: Purpose-built alpine headwater observatory in the San Juan Mountains, Colorado, with multiple co-located plots (Senator Beck alpine, Swamp Angel subalpine, Putney) instrumented for integrated snow/weather/hydrology monitoring since the early 2000s.
datasets.variables: Snow depth, SWE, air temp, RH, wind speed/dir, radiation, precipitation, streamflow
datasets.density: A handful of plots within a single small basin (sub-km to a few km spacing) — dense but small-N; requires contacting CSAS for full dataset access despite public archive page

datasets.name: Niwot Ridge LTER
datasets.description: NSF Long-Term Ecological Research site (est. 1980) in the Colorado Front Range with long-term climate stations across an elevation gradient (subalpine C1, ridge-top Saddle, alpine D1) plus 350+ archived datasets.
datasets.variables: Air temperature, precipitation, RH, wind speed, incoming shortwave radiation
datasets.density: Only 3 primary climate stations (C1, Saddle, D1) spanning several km across an elevation/terrain gradient — good long-term quality but too sparse alone for sub-5km terrain learning; useful combined with NEON NIWO co-location

datasets.name: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network)
datasets.description: NSF-funded continental network of standardized terrestrial field sites including several in complex mountain terrain (e.g., Niwot Ridge NIWO, Soaproot Saddle SOAP in the Sierra Nevada), each with co-located meteorological, soil and flux tower instrumentation.
datasets.variables: Temperature, RH, precipitation, wind speed/direction, barometric pressure, radiation, soil heat flux, eddy-covariance fluxes
datasets.density: Single well-instrumented tower + auxiliary sensor network per site (sub-km cluster of sensors) but sites are hundreds of km apart from each other — good for micrometeorology/terrain-flux physics at one location, not for multi-station spatial-density training

datasets.name: SNOTEL Network (USDA NRCS)
datasets.description: Automated snow/climate monitoring network across 12 western US states, established for water-supply forecasting; long, consistent period of record (1980-present) accessible via a REST API.
datasets.variables: Snow water equivalent (SWE), snow depth, air temperature, precipitation
datasets.density: ~900 stations across the western US mountains; regionally clustered but typically >5km apart individually — best used aggregated with CAIC/ski-area/CDOT stations for denser Colorado-specific coverage

datasets.name: Colorado Avalanche Information Center (CAIC) Weather Station Map
datasets.description: A newly launched (Jan 2026) aggregator map/API combining hundreds of weather stations across Colorado from multiple operators — ski areas, SNOTEL, CDOT (highway dept.), and CAIC's own network — into one public real-time display.
datasets.variables: Temperature, dewpoint, RH, wind speed/direction, precipitation, snow depth, SWE
datasets.density: Hundreds of stations statewide from combined networks — likely the best US candidate for finding clusters within 1-5km given multi-operator aggregation in popular mountain corridors (I-70 corridor, ski areas)

datasets.name: WFIP2 - Second Wind Forecast Improvement Project
datasets.description: DOE/NOAA-funded field campaign (Sept 2015-Feb 2017) in the Columbia River Gorge complex terrain (WA/OR), deploying a dense multi-instrument observation network (towers, sonic anemometers, lidar, radar, radiosondes) at 'supersites' specifically to characterize gap flows, mountain waves/wakes, and turbine wakes.
datasets.variables: 3D wind (multiple heights), turbulence, temperature, humidity, pressure, surface energy balance, turbine wake structure
datasets.density: Dense multi-instrument 'supersites' with sub-km to few-km spacing across the study domain — purpose-built for complex-terrain physics but limited to ~18 months of campaign data, not a long climatology

datasets.name: T-REX (Terrain-induced Rotor Experiment)
datasets.description: NCAR/EOL field campaign in Owens Valley, California studying mountain waves and rotors using dense arrays of surface meteorological towers, microbarographs, flux towers, and remote sensing.
datasets.variables: Surface pressure, temperature, wind, turbulence fluxes, boundary-layer structure
datasets.density: Dense array design explicitly for resolving sub-km to few-km terrain-flow features; short intensive-observation-period campaign (weeks), not multi-year

datasets.name: ALEX17 (Alaiz Experiment)
datasets.description: DTU/CENER field campaign at the Alaiz test site (Navarre, Spain), a 1000m-elevation mountain ridge, with a 118m instrumented met mast (9 measurement levels, sonic + cup anemometers) plus surrounding towers.
datasets.variables: Wind speed/direction at multiple heights, turbulent fluxes, temperature
datasets.density: Single primary mast plus a small number of surrounding instruments in complex topography — good vertical density, limited horizontal spatial density

datasets.name: WINSENT Complex Terrain Benchmark
datasets.description: IEA Wind Task 57 benchmark dataset from the WINSENT wind-turbine test site (Germany), providing terrain data plus measurement data (including UAV-based ANDroMeDA measurements) for validating CFD wind-flow simulations from valley to ridge test site.
datasets.variables: Wind speed/direction, turbulence, terrain/CFD mesh data
datasets.density: Purpose-built dense complex-terrain benchmark (valley-to-ridge), explicitly designed for ML/CFD model validation rather than operational climatology

datasets.name: Olostunturi Cold-Climate Wind Farm (Finland)
datasets.description: Six years of open-access meteorological mast and multi-turbine operational data from a complex-terrain wind farm in Finland with severe icing conditions.
datasets.variables: Wind speed/direction, icing indicators, turbine operational data
datasets.density: Single mast plus multiple turbine locations within the wind farm footprint (sub-km to ~1-2km spacing) — good for wind-farm-scale terrain effects and icing physics

datasets.name: Coastal Highway E39 Tall Masts (Norway)
datasets.description: High-frequency wind observations from several 50-100m tall masts in complex fjord terrain near Halsafjorden, Julsundet and Storfjorden for a Norwegian bridge engineering project.
datasets.variables: 3D wind vector at multiple heights, high-frequency turbulence
datasets.density: Several masts distributed across fjord/complex coastal terrain — moderate spatial density, strong vertical/turbulence resolution

datasets.name: NREL WIND Toolkit / WTK-LED
datasets.description: Model-derived (WRF-based) high-resolution wind time-series dataset at every modeling grid point with many vertical layers in the boundary layer; complements (not replaces) station observations. NREL NWTC M2 Tower (Boulder, CO) provides real observational tower data at the foot of the Rockies.
datasets.variables: Wind speed/direction profiles, temperature, pressure, stability parameters
datasets.density: WTK-LED is a gridded model product (not sparse stations) usable as physically-consistent labels/covariates; M2 tower is a single well-instrumented real site

datasets.name: SAFRAN-SURFEX/Crocus-MEPRA S2M Reanalysis (Meteo-France)
datasets.description: Massif-resolved meteorological and snow-cover reanalysis for the French Alps, Pyrenees and Corsica, 1958-2021, combining NWP model background (ERA-40/ARPEGE) with station observations via optimal interpolation at the scale of elevation/slope/aspect-defined 'massifs'.
datasets.variables: Temperature, precipitation (rain/snow), wind, radiation, humidity, plus modeled snowpack (depth, SWE, stability)
datasets.density: Not raw station density — a physically-consistent reanalysis at massif resolution (tens of massifs covering the French mountains); valuable as terrain-aware labels/training targets rather than as sparse point observations

datasets.name: SIM2 (Safran-Isba) Daily Surface Dataset
datasets.description: Daily gridded (8km x 8km) surface water/energy balance and meteorological output from Meteo-France's SAFRAN-ISBA land-surface model chain, freely distributed via meteo.data.gouv.fr / data.gouv.fr.
datasets.variables: Surface atmospheric parameters, soil water balance
datasets.density: 8km regular grid nationwide — coarser than needed for sub-5km terrain physics on its own but useful as a national-scale covariate/baseline

datasets.name: EVK2CNR Pyramid Meteorological Network
datasets.description: High-altitude meteorological network around Mt. Everest / Khumbu region (Nepal), operated by Italy's EVK2CNR, providing long-term extreme-elevation observations.
datasets.variables: Temperature, precipitation, wind, radiation, pressure (extreme-altitude conditions)
datasets.density: Small number of stations across the Khumbu region — sparse but scientifically unique for extreme-elevation Himalayan terrain physics

datasets.name: Tibetan Plateau 15-Station Land-Atmosphere Network
datasets.description: A coordinated 15-station network (2021-2024) spanning environmental gradients of the Tibetan Plateau, designed to address fragmented spatial coverage in prior Plateau observations.
datasets.variables: Land-atmosphere interaction variables (turbulent fluxes, radiation, soil-atmosphere exchange, standard met)
datasets.density: 15 stations across a plateau-scale gradient — coordinated but not sub-5km dense; useful for large-elevation-gradient physics rather than local terrain complexity

datasets.name: WindNinja Field Validation Datasets (Big Southern Butte / Salmon River Canyon)
datasets.description: US Forest Service field campaigns collecting high-resolution wind observations specifically to validate the WindNinja terrain wind-flow model, including a dense sonic-anemometer/lidar array over a ridge-valley-ridge system.
datasets.variables: Wind speed/direction, turbulence kinetic energy (sonic anemometers, lidar)
datasets.density: Dense instrument arrays purpose-built for resolving terrain-induced wind features at sub-km scale over short field campaigns

datasets.name: Hugging Face wind-cfd-trial (synthetic)
datasets.description: Large-scale dataset of steady-state RANS CFD wind-flow simulations over ~1000 real-world complex-terrain locations (2 wind directions each, ~10,000 total cases), explicitly built for training ML models for wind resource assessment/terrain flow.
datasets.variables: 3D simulated wind field over real terrain grids
datasets.density: Not observational — synthetic CFD-derived dense 3D wind fields; useful as physics-consistent pretraining/augmentation data alongside real sparse station networks

datasets.name: ERA5 (ECMWF Reanalysis)
datasets.description: Global atmospheric reanalysis, hourly, ~31km native resolution (0.25deg), 1940-present; not dense in mountain terrain but a standard physically-consistent baseline/covariate source, including an ARCO cloud-optimized version.
datasets.variables: Full atmospheric, land-surface and near-surface variable set
datasets.density: Coarse grid (~30km) — far too coarse alone for sub-5km terrain physics, but a near-universal covariate/label source to pair with dense station networks

datasets.name: eHYD Austria Hydrographic Network
datasets.description: Austrian hydrographic data portal with ~700 precipitation, runoff and groundwater measuring sites nationwide, CC BY 4.0 licensed.
datasets.variables: Precipitation, streamflow/runoff, groundwater level
datasets.density: ~700 sites nationally — precipitation-focused complement to GeoSphere's temperature/wind network, useful for cross-referencing orographic precipitation physics

datasets.name: Ski Resort Aggregator APIs (Snowdata.ai, SnowSure.ai, Lake Louise API, MtnManager)
datasets.description: Third-party/commercial APIs aggregating publicly reported resort conditions (snow depth, base depth, lift status) across hundreds of ski resorts worldwide, plus resort-specific weather-station APIs (e.g. Lake Louise).
datasets.variables: Snow depth/base depth, lift/terrain status, some resort weather (temp, wind)
datasets.density: Resort-level granularity (per-resort, not per-station-cluster); most require authentication/subscription for full station-level access and reporting is often self-reported rather than instrumented — lower reliability for physics training than research networks

result.dimension: Dense mountain weather observation datasets for training a terrain-weather physics model
implications: Best single ready-to-use ML dataset: PeakWeather (MeteoSwiss) — 302 complex-terrain stations, 10-min resolution, 8+ years, already packaged with per-station topographic indices specifically for spatiotemporal deep learning; start here for a working baseline before adding density from other sources.

Densest true observational network found: WegenerNet (Austria) at ~1km average station spacing (155 stations/~350km2 Feldbach region + a smaller Gesäuse mountain extension) — the only network in this search that natively satisfies the 1-5km spatial-density requirement over a sustained multi-year period; note Feldbach itself is Alpine foreland (hilly, not high-complexity terrain), so the Gesäuse extension is the more terrain-relevant subset.

Swiss IMIS (SLF) is the best large-scale high-elevation alpine network (180-200 stations across the whole Alps, live+historical API, CC BY 4.0) but its national average spacing exceeds 5km; sub-5km density only appears in specific massif/ski-area clusters — worth checking a per-station distance matrix before assuming blanket density.

Reynolds Creek's 21TB gridded hourly 10m-DEM product (kriging-interpolated from 35 stations over a 238km2 basin) is a strong candidate for directly learning terrain-driven downscaling physics because the terrain-station relationship is already explicit and spatially continuous, unlike raw sparse point data.

For validation/physics-grounding rather than climatological training, short intensive field campaigns (WFIP2 Columbia Gorge, T-REX Owens Valley, ALEX17 Spain, WINSENT Germany, WindNinja Big Southern Butte/Salmon River Canyon) provide genuinely dense (sub-km to few-km) multi-instrument arrays purpose-built to resolve terrain-induced flow — ideal for testing whether a model has learned real terrain physics, even though each covers only weeks to ~2 years.

Synthetic/CFD datasets (WINSENT, Hugging Face wind-cfd-trial ~10,000 simulated cases, FuXi-CFD's training corpus) can supplement sparse real networks by supplying dense, physically-simulated 3D wind fields over real terrain at 30m resolution — useful for pretraining or augmentation where station density is insufficient.

National networks with open APIs and good density for aggregation include GeoSphere Austria (250+ stations, one of the world's densest national networks), MeteoSwiss SwissMetNet (~160 stations, STAC API), and the newly-aggregated EEAR-Clim pan-Alpine dataset (2024-2025) which merges multiple national networks to push density higher than any single country's network alone — EEAR-Clim in particular is worth a direct read of its station list/metadata to check actual inter-station distances.

In the US, no single network matches European Alpine density; the best strategy is combining SNOTEL (~900 stations, AWDB API) with CAIC's new (Jan 2026) multi-operator aggregator (ski areas + SNOTEL + CDOT + CAIC, hundreds of stations statewide) to find sub-5km clusters, especially along the I-70 corridor and around major ski areas.

Reanalysis products (SAFRAN-SURFEX S2M for the French Alps at massif resolution, ERA5 globally at ~30km, SIM2 at 8km) are not dense observation networks but are valuable as physically-consistent labels/covariates to pair with sparse real stations, since SAFRAN in particular already encodes elevation/slope/aspect-aware interpolation — essentially a hand-engineered version of the terrain-weather physics being targeted.

Next step recommended: pull actual station coordinate lists (already available via APIs for IMIS, SwissMetNet/PeakWeather, GeoSphere, WegenerNet, SNOTEL) and compute real nearest-neighbor distance histograms per network rather than relying on network-average spacing, since several networks (IMIS, GeoSphere, SNOTEL, CAIC-aggregated) likely contain sub-5km sub-clusters even where their national average spacing is much larger.

key_findings.finding: WegenerNet (Austria) is the densest genuine long-term in-situ weather network identified, with ~1km average station spacing (155 stations over ~350 km2 in the Feldbach region) plus a smaller Gesäuse mountain-region extension, and was explicitly engineered to resolve the 1-10km spatial scale.
key_findings.source: wegenernet.org, AMS BAMS paper (doi 10.1175/bams-d-11-00161.1), ESSD doi 10.5194/essd-13-1307-2021

key_findings.finding: PeakWeather is a purpose-built, already-published ML benchmark dataset from MeteoSwiss's station network (302 complex-terrain stations, 10-min data, 8+ years) that ships with per-station topographic indices specifically for spatiotemporal/terrain-aware deep learning — the most directly usable dataset for this project's stated purpose.
key_findings.source: github.com/MeteoSwiss/PeakWeather, arXiv:2506.13652

key_findings.finding: Swiss IMIS (SLF) comprises ~180-200 automatic high-alpine stations with a fully public, unauthenticated live API (measurement-api.slf.ch) plus historical data via EnviDat (CC BY 4.0), but national-average spacing exceeds 5km even though local clusters (ski areas, massifs) may be denser.
key_findings.source: measurement-api.slf.ch, envidat.ch/dataset/imis-measuring-network, slf.ch data service page

key_findings.finding: Reynolds Creek Experimental Watershed offers a published 21TB hourly gridded product (10m LiDAR DEM, detrended kriging from 35 stations over a 238 km2 basin, 40-year record) that already encodes terrain-aware spatial interpolation, making it a strong candidate as a terrain-weather-physics training target rather than raw sparse observations.
key_findings.source: ESSD doi 10.5194/essd-10-1197-2018 (31 years of hourly spatially-distributed data), USDA ARS RCEW page

key_findings.finding: Purpose-built complex-terrain field campaigns (WFIP2 in the Columbia Gorge, T-REX in Owens Valley, ALEX17 in Spain, WINSENT in Germany, WindNinja's Big Southern Butte/Salmon River Canyon campaigns) provide genuinely dense (sub-km to few-km) multi-instrument observation arrays specifically designed to resolve terrain-induced flow, but each spans only weeks to ~2 years rather than a multi-year climatology.
key_findings.source: AMS BAMS 2019 (WFIP2), NCAR/EOL T-REX archive, DTU/windlab.hlrs.de (ALEX17), Zenodo (WINSENT), ninjastorm.firelab.org

key_findings.finding: No single US network matches European Alpine density; combining SNOTEL (~900 stations, free AWDB REST API) with Colorado's newly launched (Jan 2026) CAIC multi-operator station aggregator (ski areas + SNOTEL + CDOT + CAIC) is the best path to finding sub-5km US mountain station clusters.
key_findings.source: nrcs.usda.gov SNOTEL pages, avalanche.state.co.us weather-stations, KUNC/PostIndependent news coverage of the Jan 2026 CAIC map launch

key_findings.finding: SAFRAN-SURFEX/Crocus S2M reanalysis (French Alps/Pyrenees/Corsica, 1958-2021) is not a dense station network but a massif-resolved, terrain-aware (elevation/slope/aspect) reanalysis that could serve as a physically-consistent training label or covariate, effectively embedding hand-built terrain-weather physics already.
key_findings.source: ESSD doi 10.5194/essd-14-1707-2022, cnrm.sedoo.fr/s2m/

key_findings.finding: A newly published (2024-2025) harmonized dataset, EEAR-Clim, aggregates multiple national/regional Alpine station networks into one dense pan-Alpine daily product, potentially exceeding any single national network's density — worth direct investigation of its station metadata for actual inter-station distances.
key_findings.source: ESSD doi 10.5194/essd-17-1367-2025, EGU24-13294 abstract

key_findings.finding: Synthetic/CFD-generated datasets (Hugging Face wind-cfd-trial with ~10,000 RANS simulation cases over ~1000 real terrain locations; WINSENT's CFD mesh/validation data; the FuXi-CFD training corpus) can supplement sparse real station networks with dense, physically simulated 3D wind fields at 30m resolution, useful for pretraining or augmentation.
key_findings.source: huggingface.co/datasets/souravsud/wind-cfd-trial, Nature Communications FuXi-CFD paper, arXiv:2505.12732

key_findings.finding: Ski resort weather data is largely mediated through commercial/aggregator APIs (Snowdata.ai, SnowSure.ai, MtnManager, individual resort APIs like Lake Louise) with resort-level rather than dense multi-station granularity, and often requires authentication for full access — lower value for this project than the research/government networks found.
key_findings.source: snowdata.ai/for-developers, snowsure.ai/developers, api.skilouise.com/docs

models.name: FuXi-CFD
models.description: ML-based downscaling framework that generates detailed 3D near-surface wind fields at 30m horizontal resolution from coarse atmospheric inputs plus high-resolution terrain, trained on a large CFD-generated dataset spanning diverse terrain types.
models.architecture: Machine-learning downscaling model trained on CFD simulation outputs (terrain-informed)
models.transferable: Directly relevant as an architecture template for terrain-aware downscaling; the described CFD training corpus generation approach is reusable for building synthetic training data over new terrain

models.name: WindSeer
models.description: Real-time volumetric wind field prediction model designed to run on limited-compute devices (demonstrated aboard a small UAV) over complex terrain.
models.architecture: Neural network for real-time volumetric wind prediction
models.transferable: Relevant for lightweight/edge deployment of a terrain-weather physics model; architecture and training approach could inform a compute-efficient variant

models.name: Transformer-based Neural Operator for 3D Wind Fields
models.description: Transformer-based neural operator predicting 3D wind fields over complex mountainous terrain, designed to replace costly CFD mesh-based simulation while capturing sharp local terrain-induced wind variations.
models.architecture: Transformer / neural operator
models.transferable: Strong architectural reference for the core terrain-weather-physics modeling task itself

models.name: DG Model (Diffusion Graph Convolutional Network)
models.description: Spatiotemporal model combining diffusion graph convolution with residual learning for interpolating meteorological fields (temperature) in complex terrain from a dense station network (198 stations), outperforming kriging and other GNN baselines.
models.architecture: Diffusion Graph Convolutional Network with residual learning
models.transferable: Directly applicable graph-based architecture for interpolating/learning from irregularly-spaced dense mountain station networks

models.name: WindNinja
models.description: Open-source terrain wind-flow model (mass-conservation solver plus an incorporated RANS CFD solver) widely used operationally for wildland fire, wind energy siting, and search-and-rescue; validated against dedicated dense field campaigns.
models.architecture: Physics-based CFD (mass-conserving diagnostic model + RANS solver)
models.transferable: Established physics baseline/benchmark to compare any learned terrain-weather model against, and its field validation datasets double as training/eval data

models.name: SAFRAN Analysis System
models.description: Optimal-interpolation-based meteorological analysis system operating at the scale of elevation/slope/aspect-defined mountain 'massifs', combining NWP background fields with station observations; the engine behind the S2M reanalysis.
models.architecture: Optimal interpolation / statistical analysis system with explicit terrain stratification
models.transferable: Conceptually valuable as a hand-engineered terrain-stratification baseline against which a learned terrain-weather physics model can be benchmarked

feasibility.rationale: No paper was found doing the exact 'train on Swiss Alps data, deploy in North American mountains' transfer for general terrain-weather prediction — this is a genuine literature gap. However, three adjacent precedents validate the core hypothesis: (1) Swiss-trained avalanche RF models transferred to the Pyrenees with ~60-70% zero-shot agreement (Bacardit et al. 2026), proving cross-range transfer works but degrades without local adaptation; (2) Sierra Nevada to Colorado Rockies SWE transfer learning improved R2 from 0.45 to 0.54-0.56 and reduced bias ~30% (El Halabi et al. 2025), confirming topographic predictors (elevation, slope, aspect) behave similarly enough across US mountain ranges for transfer to help; (3) the RainShift benchmark (Harder et al. 2026) rigorously demonstrates that geographic distribution shift degrades deep-learning downscaling models substantially, but explicit domain adaptation (quantile-mapping for zero-shot, fine-tuning for few-shot) recovers skill. The dominant 2024-2026 architecture pattern — LoRA/PEFT adapting a frozen foundation-model backbone with lightweight terrain-aware heads — makes the approach tractable without full retraining. Multiple open-weight pretrained models exist at relevant scales. The physics (mass conservation, terrain-forced flow) is well understood and constrainable. The gap is engineering integration and cross-continent validation, not fundamental science.
feasibility.precedent: Sierra Nevada -> Colorado Rockies SWE transfer (El Halabi et al. 2025, JGR ML&C): R2 +20%, bias -30% with topographic predictors. Swiss Alps -> Pyrenees avalanche model transfer (Bacardit et al. 2026, Cold Regions Sci. Tech.): ~60-70% zero-shot agreement. RainShift benchmark (Harder et al. 2026): domain adaptation recovers downscaling skill across geographic regions. DEVINE wind downscaling CNN: trained on synthetic topographies, validated on real Alpine stations. granite-geospatial-wxc-downscaling: Prithvi WxC fine-tuned for 6x temperature / 8x wind downscaling with open weights.

recommended_pretrain_data.why: Purpose-built ML benchmark: 302 complex-terrain stations, 10-min resolution, 8+ years, ships with per-station topographic indices (elevation, slope, aspect, curvature, sky-view factor) specifically for spatiotemporal deep learning. Already packaged on HuggingFace. Start here for a working baseline before adding density from other sources.
recommended_pretrain_data.accessibility: Open. GitHub: MeteoSwiss/PeakWeather, HuggingFace: MeteoSwiss/PeakWeather, arXiv:2506.13652

recommended_pretrain_data.why: The project already ingests HRRR. StormCast was trained on this exact data at 3km with dense boundary-layer vertical resolution. Using HRRR as the coarse-input conditioning signal for a terrain downscaling head means zero new data pipeline work for the backbone stage, and StormCast provides a pre-learned representation of HRRR physics.
recommended_pretrain_data.accessibility: Open. AWS S3: noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds bucket. Already integrated in the current system.

recommended_pretrain_data.why: 180-200 automatic high-alpine stations, mostly above treeline near avalanche starting zones (2000-3000m), 30-min interval. Live REST API (measurement-api.slf.ch) plus historical data on EnviDat (CC BY 4.0). The most avalanche-relevant dense station network in existence. Use to supplement PeakWeather with high-elevation avalanche-zone observations.
recommended_pretrain_data.accessibility: Open. Live API: measurement-api.slf.ch/v1 (unauthenticated). Historical: envidat.ch/dataset/imis-measuring-network (DOI 10.16904/envidat.406)

recommended_pretrain_data.dataset: Reynolds Creek Experimental Watershed gridded product
recommended_pretrain_data.why: 21TB hourly gridded product on a 10m LiDAR DEM using detrended kriging from 35 stations over 238 km2, 40-year record. The terrain-station-weather relationship is already spatially continuous and explicit — ideal for learning terrain-driven downscaling physics as supervised training pairs (coarse input -> gridded fine output over known terrain).
recommended_pretrain_data.accessibility: Open. ESSD doi 10.5194/essd-10-1197-2018. HydroShare RCCZO resources.

recommended_pretrain_data.dataset: Synthetic CFD terrain-wind data (HuggingFace wind-cfd-trial + WindNinja-generated)
recommended_pretrain_data.why: wind-cfd-trial provides ~10,000 RANS CFD simulation cases over ~1,000 real-world complex-terrain locations at 30m resolution, explicitly built for training ML terrain-wind models. Supplement with locally-generated WindNinja runs over Colorado avalanche-path DEMs to create target-domain synthetic training pairs. This is the proven DEVINE/FuXi-CFD pretraining strategy — learn terrain physics from physics simulators, not sparse stations.
recommended_pretrain_data.accessibility: Open. HuggingFace: souravsud/wind-cfd-trial. WindNinja: public domain, pip install windninjapy.

recommended_pretrain_data.why: Massif-resolved, terrain-aware (elevation/slope/aspect) meteorological and snow-cover reanalysis, 1958-2021. Already encodes hand-built terrain-weather physics stratified by terrain attributes. Use as physically-consistent training labels or as a benchmark to validate whether a learned model recovers the same terrain-weather relationships that operational meteorologists encoded manually.

recommended_pretrain_data.dataset: SNOTEL + CAIC multi-operator aggregator (Colorado target domain)
recommended_pretrain_data.why: 118 SNOTEL stations in current system plus CAIC's Jan 2026 aggregator (ski areas + CDOT + CAIC own network, hundreds of stations). This is the fine-tuning target, not pretraining data. Compute nearest-neighbor distances to find sub-5km clusters (likely along I-70 corridor and around major ski areas) for local validation.
recommended_pretrain_data.accessibility: Open. SNOTEL: AWDB REST API. CAIC: stations.avalanche.state.co.us/zones.php

recommended_pretrain_data.dataset: WFIP2 Columbia Gorge + WindNinja field validation campaigns
recommended_pretrain_data.why: Dense (sub-km) multi-instrument arrays purpose-built to resolve terrain-induced flow: gap winds, mountain waves, wakes. Use for physics-validation testing — if the model cannot reproduce documented terrain-flow phenomena from these campaigns, it has not learned real terrain physics. Not for training (too short), but essential for evaluation.
recommended_pretrain_data.accessibility: Open. WFIP2: AMS BAMS 2019 / OSTI 1409835. WindNinja: ninjastorm.firelab.org/windninja/field/

recommended_architecture.name: StormCast backbone + DEVINE-style terrain downscaling head with LoRA adaptation
recommended_architecture.description: Two-stage architecture: (1) NVIDIA StormCast as the mesoscale backbone — the only open-weight model trained at actual terrain/mesoscale resolution (3km HRRR), with dense boundary-layer vertical resolution, 99 state variables, and a commercially-permissive license (NVIDIA Open Model License). It already understands HRRR-scale dynamics over CONUS. (2) A terrain-aware downscaling head inspired by DEVINE's U-Net architecture — takes StormCast's 3km output plus high-resolution DEM-derived terrain features (elevation, slope, aspect, curvature, Sx wind-exposure index, roughness/vegetation class) and produces sub-km wind, temperature, and precipitation fields at specific terrain locations. Mass conservation enforced as a hard architectural constraint on the wind output (divergence-free projection layer), following the JMLR hard-constrained downscaling pattern that demonstrably improves out-of-distribution generalization. The terrain encoder uses the proven minimal feature set recurring across WindNinja, WAsP, DEVINE, and PeakWeather: elevation, slope, aspect, curvature, sky-view factor, Sx upwind exposure, and roughness class — all computable from a standard DEM plus land-cover data.
recommended_architecture.pretrain_approach: Phase 1 — Synthetic terrain physics pretraining: Train the downscaling head on synthetic CFD data (HuggingFace wind-cfd-trial 10K cases + locally-generated WindNinja runs over diverse terrain) to learn general terrain-flow physics without needing dense real stations. This mirrors the proven DEVINE strategy (trained on 7,279 synthetic Gaussian topographies) and FuXi-CFD (trained on large CFD corpus). Phase 2 — Dense Alpine station training: Fine-tune on PeakWeather (302 Swiss stations, 10-min, 8+ years with topographic indices) plus Swiss IMIS high-alpine data (~180 stations), learning the statistical relationship between terrain descriptors and observed weather across a dense mountain network. Phase 3 — Reynolds Creek gridded product: Further train on the 21TB hourly 10m-grid product to learn terrain-resolved spatial patterns from a single well-instrumented catchment. Throughout, pair StormCast or ERA5 as the coarse atmospheric conditioning input.
recommended_architecture.finetune_approach: LoRA/PEFT adaptation of the frozen StormCast backbone for the Colorado domain (following the WeatherPEFT and MENA regional adaptation patterns — arXiv 2509.22020, 2409.07585). Fine-tune the terrain downscaling head on SNOTEL + CAIC aggregated Colorado stations using few-shot domain adaptation per the RainShift protocol: (1) quantile-mapping data alignment between Alpine and Rockies climate distributions for zero-shot baseline, (2) few-shot fine-tuning on the densest Colorado station clusters (I-70 corridor, ski areas where sub-5km spacing exists), (3) evaluate on held-out Colorado stations. Expected baseline: ~60-70% skill retention from zero-shot transfer (per Alps-to-Pyrenees precedent), improving to ~80-85% with few-shot fine-tuning (per Sierra-Nevada-to-Rockies SWE precedent of +20% R2 gain). Add mass conservation loss term during fine-tuning to improve out-of-distribution generalization to unseen Colorado terrain.
recommended_architecture.precedent: StormCast: trained on HRRR 3km, open weights on HuggingFace (nvidia/stormcast-v1-era5-hrrr), NVIDIA Open Model License. DEVINE: U-Net wind downscaling to 30m over complex terrain, pretrained weights on Zenodo, purpose-built for snow-transport/avalanche applications. WeatherPEFT (ICLR 2026): LoRA adapters on weather foundation models for regional specialization. Global-to-Local framework (arXiv 2607.03279): lightweight prediction heads on frozen backbone achieve ~100x resolution increase. Hard-Constrained Deep Learning for Climate Downscaling (JMLR 24(365)): architectural conservation constraints improve OOD generalization.

existing_models.name: NVIDIA StormCast
existing_models.what_it_does: Autoregressively predicts 99 state variables at 3km resolution over CONUS, trained on HRRR data with dense boundary-layer vertical resolution and 1-hour timestep. Diffusion-based mesoscale model.
existing_models.how_we_use_it: Primary backbone. Already operates at near-terrain-scale (3km) over CONUS including Colorado. Freeze most parameters, apply LoRA adapters for Colorado-specific fine-tuning, and attach a terrain downscaling head for sub-km output. Its HRRR training means it already understands the same data our system ingests.

existing_models.name: DEVINE (wind_downscaling_cnn)
existing_models.what_it_does: Fully convolutional U-Net that downscales NWP wind fields to 30m resolution over complex mountain terrain, conditioned on DEM-derived topographic features. Purpose-built for wind-driven snow transport and avalanche-relevant nivology.
existing_models.how_we_use_it: Architecture template and potential weight initialization for the terrain downscaling head. Clone the repo, evaluate pretrained weights on Colorado terrain/wind data, and adapt the U-Net architecture for our multi-variable (wind + temperature + precipitation) downscaling head. The closest existing domain match to our target application.

existing_models.name: FuXi-CFD
existing_models.what_it_does: Generates 3D near-surface wind fields at 30m horizontal resolution from coarse atmospheric inputs plus high-resolution terrain, capturing slope jets, flow deflection, and recirculation that km-scale models average out.
existing_models.how_we_use_it: Inference-only evaluation — download the ONNX model from HuggingFace, run it over Colorado avalanche terrain DEMs with HRRR boundary conditions, and use its output as (a) a baseline to beat, (b) potential pseudo-labels for terrain-wind training data generation, and (c) an architecture reference. Cannot fine-tune (ONNX only), but can distill from.

existing_models.name: ECMWF AIFS
existing_models.what_it_does: ECMWF's operational AI Forecasting System — encoder-processor-decoder model comparable to GraphCast/Pangu, produced by the agency that generates ERA5/HRES reference data.
existing_models.how_we_use_it: Alternative backbone if StormCast proves insufficient. Fully open CC BY 4.0 license (most permissive of all top-tier global models), and comes from the same institution producing the verification data — lowest distribution-shift risk. Use as global-scale input conditioning if we need synoptic-scale context beyond HRRR's CONUS domain.

existing_models.name: granite-geospatial-wxc-downscaling (Prithvi WxC fine-tuned)
existing_models.what_it_does: IBM/NASA fine-tuned version of Prithvi WxC foundation model for 6x temperature and 8x wind downscaling, validated on MERRA-2, ECCC data, and EURO-CORDEX climate simulations.
existing_models.how_we_use_it: Direct comparison baseline — this is the closest existing open-weight model to what we are building (foundation model fine-tuned specifically for weather downscaling). Evaluate it on Colorado stations to establish what a foundation-model-downscaling approach achieves out of the box before investing in custom training.

existing_models.name: SNOWstorm
existing_models.what_it_does: Deep-learning emulator (multiple U-Nets) trained on 50m LES that predicts near-surface wind, snow mass change rate, sublimation rate, and snow transport flux — the full wind-driven snow redistribution chain, not just wind.
existing_models.how_we_use_it: Evaluate for the wind-loading / snow-redistribution vertical specifically — its output variables (snow mass change, transport flux) map more directly onto avalanche-relevant quantities (windslab loading) than raw wind speed. Investigate whether its intermediate wind-field predictions can serve as initialization or auxiliary targets for our terrain head.

existing_models.name: NVIDIA FourCastNet3 (SFNO)
existing_models.what_it_does: Global probabilistic ensemble weather forecasting using Spherical Fourier Neural Operator attention, Apache 2.0 licensed.
existing_models.how_we_use_it: Feature extractor — the AFNO/SFNO attention blocks are architecturally simple and liftable as a reusable spectral-attention encoder. If we build a custom backbone rather than using StormCast, FourCastNet's SFNO blocks are the cleanest open building block for a Fourier-domain terrain-weather encoder.

existing_models.name: WindNinja
existing_models.what_it_does: Open-source (public domain) terrain wind-flow model with mass-conserving and RANS CFD solvers, widely used operationally for wildfire, wind energy, and search-and-rescue. Python bindings available (windninjapy).
existing_models.how_we_use_it: Not a neural model — use as (a) a synthetic training-data generator: run WindNinja over Colorado avalanche-path DEMs to create terrain-to-wind-field training pairs, (b) a physics baseline to benchmark our learned model against, and (c) a reference for the proven minimal terrain-feature schema (DEM + vegetation/roughness + initial wind).

result.novel_approach: Pair NASA/IBM Prithvi-EO (geospatial/land-cover foundation model trained on Harmonized Landsat/Sentinel-2 imagery) as a terrain encoder with a weather backbone (StormCast or AIFS), following arXiv 2608.12271 which demonstrated that earth-observation foundation-model embeddings used as sub-grid terrain/land-surface descriptors to condition a downscaling model outperform hand-engineered terrain features. This cross-domain pairing — a computer-vision model trained on satellite imagery providing the 'what does this terrain look like' representation, fused with an atmospheric model providing the 'what is the weather doing' representation — is the most creative architecture the research surfaced. It sidesteps the terrain-feature-engineering problem entirely: instead of manually computing slope, aspect, curvature, sky-view factor, and roughness from DEMs, let a pretrained vision model learn what terrain features matter for weather from raw satellite imagery. The Prithvi-EO weights are open (Apache-style), and the approach has been validated in at least one published downscaling study but never applied to avalanche terrain-weather prediction specifically.
risks: Domain shift between European Alps and Colorado Rockies is real and quantified: the best available precedent (Alps-to-Pyrenees avalanche transfer) shows ~30-40% accuracy degradation from zero-shot cross-range transfer due to different snow climate regimes, terrain geometry scales, and continental vs. maritime influence patterns. Budget for explicit domain adaptation, not just hope.

Station density in Colorado (~118 SNOTEL + CAIC aggregated stations) may be insufficient for meaningful fine-tuning — the dense Alpine networks have 180-300+ stations in much smaller areas. Compute actual nearest-neighbor distance histograms for Colorado stations before assuming sub-5km clusters exist; if they do not, fine-tuning signal will be weak.

Orographic precipitation ML is significantly less mature than wind downscaling — the literature is still largely correlational/statistical (CNN downscaling, radar+DEM kernels) rather than physics-constrained. Wind and temperature transfer may work well while precipitation (critical for avalanche forecasting) lags behind.

Safety-critical application risk: avalanche forecasting is life-safety. A model that appears to work on average but fails on the specific terrain configurations and weather patterns that produce dangerous avalanches (wind-loaded leeward slopes, temperature inversions in starting zones) could be worse than no model at all. Evaluation must focus on the dangerous tail, not average skill.

License ambiguity on key models: Aurora weights are listed as 'Other' license requiring Microsoft contact for commercial use; GraphCast/GenCast weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial only). If the terrain-weather API has any commercial angle, the usable model set narrows to StormCast, FourCastNet3, AIFS, and ClimaX. Confirm licenses before investing training compute.

Synthetic CFD training data (DEVINE-style, WindNinja-generated) may not capture the full complexity of real atmospheric boundary-layer dynamics over terrain — CFD simplifies turbulence (RANS steady-state vs. real transient flow), omits moisture/precipitation entirely, and assumes idealized boundary conditions. Models pretrained on synthetic data alone will need real-observation fine-tuning.

Computational cost of fine-tuning billion-parameter foundation models (Prithvi-WxC is 2.3B parameters, Aurora is comparable) may exceed project resources even with LoRA/PEFT. StormCast's model size should be evaluated against available GPU memory before committing.

Validation paradox: the whole point is predicting weather where stations do not exist, but validation requires ground truth at those locations. Short-term field campaigns (like WFIP2 or T-REX) provide sub-km validation data but only for weeks, not climatological periods. Plan for leave-one-station-out cross-validation on existing networks as the primary evaluation, supplemented by physics-consistency checks (mass conservation, terrain-flow phenomenology).

The hyperlocal weather API market ($4.35B by 2034) is attractive but monetization is explicitly flagged as harder than forecast quality (per WindBorne Systems coverage). Building a technically excellent terrain-weather model does not guarantee a viable business without a clear go-to-market for specific verticals.
